A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same NuRL study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including v2's added Appendices F and G.

before.justification: V1 reports original training and evaluation results across three models and six benchmarks, including hint ablations, self-consistency experiments and pass@k analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds harder-benchmark evaluations, Qwen self-consistency results and a qualitative comparison of trained model outputs.

M1.justification: The two-stage GRPO framework, offline abstract-hint generation, failure-triggered augmentation of G-1 rollouts and hint-free inference remain unchanged. Removing the eight-hint sampling description does not establish an actual procedure change.

E1.justification: Appendix F substantially expands difficult competition and olympiad mathematics coverage through Brumo, CMIMC, HMMT February/November and OlymMATH Easy/Hard, while retaining the original benchmarks. Table 6 also reports AIME results, but does not identify that set's year.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains zero-shot, few-shot, RFT, ReFT and GRPO comparisons. The added evaluations reuse existing comparators and NuRL variants; newly cited approaches are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 3 extends the 16-sample self-consistency experiment from Llama and OctoThinker to Qwen3-4B. The reported training budgets, token limits, temperatures and Appendix B configurations for retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The self-consistency analysis gains Qwen results, and Appendix G adds a trigonometry case comparing an incorrect GRPO answer with a correct NuRL solution. Existing hint-type, training-stage, difficulty-trigger and solvability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over 16 runs, except three runs for MMLU-Pro. V2 introduces no changed run-count policy, seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds substantial results in the harder-math regime: Qwen averages 41.74 for GRPO, 42.85 for self-hint NuRL and 44.43 for teacher-hint NuRL. Results are mixed in some settings, including Llama's teacher-hint average of 4.00 versus GRPO's 4.01. Figure 3 and Appendix G add further findings; shared Tables 1 and 2 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, normalized-advantage equations and zero-reward argument are unchanged. Appendix G's added algebra is part of an illustrative model-output example.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: selective abstract hints enable learning from otherwise unsuccessful problems, improve reasoning performance and complement test-time scaling. The additional evaluations support these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix F extends the applicability interpretation to substantially harder reasoning benchmarks, describing the gains as reliable. Its broad superiority wording does not discuss individual regressions visible in Table 6. Existing mechanism explanations and hallucination limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit NuRL repository link and identifies MATH 500 as Figure 3's dataset. It removes v1's explanation of generating eight hints per question and randomly selecting among them. Hardware, appendix hyperparameters and hint-generation prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of self-reflection, TBA and further hint-based approaches, including Questa and RLAD, while removing the Step-back Prompting connection and citation. MathArena and OlymMATH references accompany the new evaluations. The central positioning around self-generated hints without an SFT stage remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording edits, rewrites part of related work and adds Appendices F and G. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains Qwen bars, an expanded legend and a revised vertical scale. V2 adds Table 6 and boxed model outputs, redistributes appendix tables and introduces conference headers. Most existing displays retain their design.

improvement.justification: The harder-math evaluations and added Qwen self-consistency analysis modestly strengthen evidence for the retained claims beyond v1's coverage. The benefit is limited by incomplete identification of the new benchmark versions, removal of eight-hint sampling details and Table 6's broad superiority wording despite individual regressions. The core method and original results remain unchanged.
